test_title: PYST 5: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements best explains why hormonal contraceptive pills can have side effects?

options.text: They interfere with the body’s immune system.
They destroy the egg inside the ovary.
They disrupt the natural hormonal balance, affecting other physiological functions.
They prevent the sperm from reaching the egg mechanically.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They disrupt the natural hormonal balance, affecting other physiological functions.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hormonal contraceptive pills** work by introducing synthetic hormones like estrogen and progestin into the body, which mimic natural hormones to prevent pregnancy.
 
• These synthetic hormones can **disrupt the body's natural hormonal balance**, affecting processes such as ovulation, menstrual cycles, and other physiological functions.
 
• By altering hormone levels, contraceptive pills can cause **side effects such as mood swings, nausea, headaches, weight changes, and changes in libido.**
 
• The hormonal disruption may also affect other systems, such as the **cardiovascular system**, increasing the risk of blood clots in some individuals.
 
• Hormonal contraceptives may affect natural hormone production over time, leading to potential long-term effects, such as irregular periods after discontinuation. ***Hence, the correct answer is: They disrupt the natural hormonal balance, affecting other physiological functions.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Hormonal Contraceptives:**

 
 
• Hormonal contraceptives work by **preventing ovulation**, thickening cervical mucus to block sperm entry, or altering the uterine lining to prevent implantation.
 
• The pills often contain a combination of **estrogen and progestin**, or only progestin, depending on the type.
 
 
 
• **Common Side Effects:**
 
 
• Common side effects include **spotting between periods, breast tenderness, nausea, and weight gain.**
 
• Long-term use may increase the risk of **hypertension, blood clots, or stroke** in individuals with predisposing factors.
 
 
 
• **Non-Hormonal Contraceptive Methods:**
 
 
• Non-hormonal methods such as **condoms, copper IUDs, or diaphragms** work mechanically or chemically without altering hormonal balance.
 
• These methods are preferred by individuals who want to avoid hormonal side effects or have contraindications for hormonal contraceptives.
 
 
 
• **Contraindications for Hormonal Contraceptives:**
 
 
• Hormonal contraceptives are contraindicated in individuals with a history of **blood clots, stroke, breast cancer, or uncontrolled hypertension.**
 
• They are also not recommended for smokers over the age of 35 due to increased cardiovascular risks.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The first oral contraceptive pill was approved by the **FDA in 1960**, revolutionizing reproductive health and family planning globally.
 
• Modern contraceptives are more refined, with lower doses of hormones to reduce side effects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1: They interfere with the body’s immune system.**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect as hormonal contraceptives primarily affect the reproductive system and hormonal balance rather than directly interfering with the immune system.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: They destroy the egg inside the ovary.**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because hormonal contraceptives prevent ovulation rather than destroying eggs.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: They prevent the sperm from reaching the egg mechanically.**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because hormonal pills work chemically by altering hormones, not mechanically.
 
 
 
• **Global Statistics:**
 
 
• As per the **WHO**, approximately **214 million women** globally use hormonal contraceptives.
 
• Hormonal contraceptives are widely used due to their **high efficacy rates**, ranging from 91% to 99% when used correctly.
